terms.meaning: A place that gives an organism the right conditions to live and grow.
The living things in a habitat.
The non-living things in a habitat, such as air, water and sunlight.
A group of individuals of the same species in a habitat at one time.
Different populations living together in one habitat.
A community together with the non-living parts of its area, all interacting.
A fungus or bacterium that breaks dead things into simple nutrients for the soil.

items.name: Mutualism
items.example: Bees get nectar and flowers get pollinated.

items.name: Commensalism
items.formula: One benefits, and the other is neither helped nor harmed.
items.example: An orchid grows on a tree branch for support.

items.name: Parasitism
items.formula: One benefits while living on or in a host, and the host is harmed.
items.example: A tick on a dog, or a roundworm in the intestine.

items.name: Predation
items.formula: One organism hunts and eats another.

items.name: Competition
items.formula: Organisms struggle for the same limited resources.
items.example: Trees competing for sunlight, or birds for nest sites.

items.name: Effects that spread
items.formula: Change one part and others change too.
items.example: Fish eat dragonfly young, so more bees survive and shore plants make more seeds.

items.name: Producers
items.formula: Green plants and algae, which make their own food.

items.name: Consumers
items.formula: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, and omnivores eat both.

items.name: Food chain
items.formula: A line of who eats whom, starting from a producer.

items.name: Food web
items.formula: Food chains linked together, because most organisms eat or are eaten by several others.
items.example: A frog may eat many insects and be eaten by a snake or a bird.

items.name: Kinds of ecosystem
items.example: A pond, a forest and a farm.

items.name: Mangroves
items.formula: They slow down storms and floods, and they absorb carbon dioxide.
items.example: The Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

items.name: Protected areas
items.formula: National parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves.
items.example: Jim Corbett and Manas are national parks, and the Nilgiris is a biosphere reserve.

items.name: Farming with care
items.formula: Too many chemicals harm the soil. Compost, crop variety and natural methods help.
items.example: Kunapa Jala is an old liquid fertiliser from fermented residues.

mistakes.text: A population is one species. A community is many species together.
In parasitism the host is harmed. In commensalism the other organism is not.
Water, soil and sunlight are part of an ecosystem too, though they are not alive.
